newsitem.title: INDIA: Cyclone to hit Indian coast by Wednesday noon.
newsitem.headline: Cyclone to hit Indian coast by Wednesday noon.

text.p: A cyclone, whipping up winds of up to 150-180 kmph (94-113 miles per hour), was likely to hit the southeastern state of Andhra Pradesh by noon on Wednesday, meteorological officials said on Tuesday.
"We expect the storm to cross the coast between Kakinada and Nellore (coastal towns) by midday tomorrow," a meterological official at the state capital Hyderabad told Reuters.
He said the storm was still stationary, located around 300 km (188 miles) southeast of Machilipatnam port lying on the coast between Kakinada and Nellore, and was gathering strength.
"It's already overcast along the coast and strong winds have started to blow," the official said.
Meteorolgical officials said they had now revised their earlier estimates of wind speed upwards. They also said the storm would hit the coast around noon, instead of during the early hours.

J.V.M Naidu, director at the cyclone warning centre at the port town of Visakhapatnam, said: "Winds up to 220 kmph (138 miles per hour) can now be expected at the places where the storm hits the coast."
He said at least 150-200 square kilometres (94-125 square miles) around the eye of the storm would be affected by heavy rains and winds.

Officials in Hyderabad said they feared the cyclone would cause greater damage than the one which devastated the coastal state in early November. That storm had also generated gale force winds of 220 kmph.
More than 2,000 people were killed or lost at sea in the storm which damaged crops and property worth more than 50 billion rupees ($1.4 billion).
Naidu said the high winds could snap electrical cables, uproot microwave towers and totally disrupt power supply and communications.
"It will lead to a total breakdown of communications which are still being restored after the previous storm," Naidu said.
He said train traffic along the east coast which had just resumed after electrical traction wires had been repaired, might collapse again under the fresh onslaught of the cyclone.
Naidu said flood waters in the low-lying areas would normally be pumped out to ensure drinking water supplies were not contaminated.
"This will not be possible if power supply is disrupted," he said. "It has already started raining in Visakhapatnam and winds of up to 50 kmph (30 miles per hour) are blowing."
Officials in Hyderabad said vast stretches along the coast, including the two districts of East and West Godavari, had overcast skies and rainfall was expected later in the night.

The two districts which had borne the brunt of the November 7 cyclone's fury were once again in the path of the latest storm. "We have already evacuated about 15,000 people from low-lying coastal areas," relief commissioner H.S. Brahma said.
Cyclone warnings had been issued and fishermen advised not to set out to the Bay of Bengal, he said.
Army and navy servicemen had been placed on alert to assist state authorities to cope with the situation with transport and medical teams, he added.
